page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Astronomical unit and light year
lines: One astronomical unit is the mean distance
between the earth and the sun.
One light year is the distance light travels
steps.why: A light year is a distance, not a time, even though the word year appears in it. Saying "the distance light travels" makes that unmistakable.
common_mistakes: Calling the light year a unit of time because of the word year.

recall.must_convey: That the astronomical unit is the mean earth to sun distance and the light year is the distance light travels in one year.
accept: distance light travels in a year

steps.memory_tip: A light year is a DISTANCE. The word year names the travel time, not the quantity.
steps.margin_note: Write "distance" in the light year line explicitly.

steps.why: The name is built from parallax and second, which is exactly what the definition says, so the name itself is the reminder.
common_mistakes: Saying a parsec is smaller than a light year. It is about 3.26 times larger.
Using the diameter of the earth’s orbit (2 AU) as the baseline. The parsec uses 1 AU, the radius; the parallax angle is the half-angle at the star. 1 parsec = 3.08 × 10¹⁶ m.

recall.must_convey: That a parsec is the distance at which one astronomical unit subtends one second of arc, and equals about 3.26 light years.
accept: three point two six light years

steps.memory_tip: PARallax + SECond = parsec. The name is the definition.
steps.margin_note: Order them AU, light year, parsec — smallest to largest.

insider_note: Three definitions, two marks. Keep each to one line and give at least one value.
